admission.justification: Realized across the lifespan callback, the watcher service that performs the stop, the metrics store and the degradation state machine, and it is the reason a distinct decision (DEC-ZS4FH6) still constrains later work. The stop's settings source is the part a reader gets wrong, so the record states it: authority settings, not the generated document. Tests cover the sample, the transition and the missing entry.

applicability: The serving application's periodic provider-metrics tick, for as long as the process lives.
conditions: Samples may be present, empty or unreadable; the tick runs regardless of launch authority and dashboard interest.
The degradation thresholds and failSafeEnabled come from the settings the tick reads.
exclusions: Any inference that an empty or revoked authority setting proves a fleet absent.
Any start, install or query path reached from the safety loop.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_l192_safety_stop_authority_settings.py (legacy entry selects the provider; no entry selects none) and test_provider_degradation.py green; the prose half of this rule is asserted by test_l192_provider_safety_prose.py, one of the two modules repaired under the scoped pyright finding with no assertion changed. No live-container stop was executed or claimed.

statement: Live periodic safety is intact and now effective: the dashboard samples, records, evaluates, compacts and, on the transition into critical under failSafeEnabled, stops a provider the authority settings enable, because the stop reads those settings instead of an empty generated document.
